title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins — opening the door to easy editing
excerpt: The model can modify existing proteins using a probability approach.
content_html:
A sci-fi weapon has entered the AI age. An artificial-intelligence tool dubbed Raygun can miniaturize or supersize a natural protein without disrupting its shape or ability to function1.

Scientists have developed a host of AI ‘protein language models’ that can create proteins from scratch. But Raygun can modify existing proteins using some of the same steps as natural evolution: adding or deleting single protein subunits or substituting one protein subunit for another.

Raygun is a “meaningful and creative” first step towards editing existing proteins, says Fajie Yuan, a computational biologist who works on protein language models at Westlake University in Hangzhou, China, who is not involved in the work. “For many real applications, that is exactly what researchers want — not a completely new protein, but a better, smaller, larger or more adaptable version of one they already trust,” he says.

The study is published today in Nature.

Protein revolution

Protein-building models are now so advanced that they can design antibodies with clinical potential. But scientists would also like to resize natural proteins — a tantalizing prospect for biotechnology applications, says study co-author Rohit Singh, a computational biologist at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. “Sometimes a smaller protein can do things or fit into places where a larger protein cannot,” he says.

But efforts to use AI systems to modify existing proteins have been limited, because they tend to change the structure or function.

I told AI to make me a protein. Here’s what it came up with

Singh and his colleagues turned to ESM-2, a large language model for protein design. Instead of text, ESM-2 and other AI-based protein models are trained on millions of protein sequences. After learning the evolutionary ‘grammar’ or patterns of these sequences, these models can generate new proteins.

Most protein language models create representations of proteins as amino-acid sequences of various lengths. But this system makes it difficult to create proteins that keep their overall structure and function at different sizes. So Raygun, which is based on ESM-2, takes a more mathematical approach: it divides each protein into pieces and translates the information in each piece into numerical patterns. The tool then uses these patterns to create a standardized version of the protein that follows particular rules. The model learns those rules, allowing it to generate the protein at various sizes without compromising its structural integrity.

content_html_zh:
科幻武器已经进入AI时代。 一种名为 Raygun 的人工智能工具可以在不破坏天然蛋白质形状或功能的情况下将其小型化或超大化。

科学家们开发了一系列人工智能“蛋白质语言模型”，可以从头开始创建蛋白质。 但 Raygun 可以使用一些与自然进化相同的步骤来修改现有的蛋白质：添加或删除单个蛋白质亚基或用一种蛋白质亚基替换另一种蛋白质亚基。

中国杭州西湖大学从事蛋白质语言模型研究的计算生物学家袁发杰（未参与这项工作）表示，Raygun 是编辑现有蛋白质的“有意义且富有创造性”的第一步。 “对于许多实际应用来说，这正是研究人员想要的——不是一种全新的蛋白质，而是他们已经信任的蛋白质的更好、更小、更大或更适应性的版本，”他说。

该研究今天发表在《自然》杂志上。

蛋白质革命

蛋白质构建模型现在非常先进，可以设计具有临床潜力的抗体。 但科学家们也希望调整天然蛋白质的大小——这对于生物技术应用来说是一个诱人的前景，该研究的合著者、北卡罗来纳州达勒姆杜克大学的计算生物学家罗希特·辛格说。 “有时，较小的蛋白质可以做一些事情或适应较大的蛋白质不能做的事情，”他说。

但使用人工智能系统修改现有蛋白质的努力受到限制，因为它们往往会改变结构或功能。

我告诉人工智能让我成为一种蛋白质。 这是它的想法

Singh 和他的同事转向 ESM-2，一种用于蛋白质设计的大型语言模型。 ESM-2 和其他基于人工智能的蛋白质模型不是基于文本，而是基于数百万个蛋白质序列进行训练。 在了解这些序列的进化“语法”或模式后，这些模型可以生成新的蛋白质。

大多数蛋白质语言模型将蛋白质表示为不同长度的氨基酸序列。 但这个系统很难创造出在不同尺寸下保持其整体结构和功能的蛋白质。 因此，基于 ESM-2 的 Raygun 采用了更加数学化的方法：它将每个蛋白质分成几块，并将每块中的信息转换为数字模式。 然后，该工具使用这些模式来创建遵循特定规则的标准化版本的蛋白质。 该模型学习这些规则，使其能够生成各种大小的蛋白质，而不损害其结构完整性。
